newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's TAB appoints Pemberton as chairman.
newsitem.headline: Australia's TAB appoints Pemberton as chairman.

text.p: State-owned betting agency TAB, which is to be floated early next year, has appointed Ian Pemberton as its chairman, TAB's owner, the New South Wales (NSW) state government.
NSW treasurer Michael Egan said the government aims to have the TAB ready for sale by December this year and to proceed to a public share offer in the first half of 1998.

Pemberton, who is also chairman of Qantas Airways Ltd, was appointed to the TAB board along with three other new directors, Belinda Hutchinson, Graham kelly and Barrie Unsworth, who was a former premier of NSW, Egan said.
The new directors will join fellow board members Geoff Wild and Ross Cribb, the former TAB chairman who will become the agency's deputy chairman. TAB chief executive is Allen Windross.

Under the new board, the TAB would expand its business beyond wagering to include the linked poker machine jackpots, monitoring gaming machines in NSW clubs and pubs and fixed odds sports betting, Egan said.
Stockbrokers Macquarie Equities said in a recent report that TAB could be worth between A$1.25 billion and A$1.4 billion.
